text: We are also seeing more organisations use AI for the public good.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, the National Parks Board is exploring an AI application named KOEL built by participants of the Build For Good Hackathon to help with biodiversity surveys using bioacoustics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: With KOEL, researchers can identify animal species from audio recordings, which can save thousands of man-hours, increase efficiency and accuracy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It is an AI-enabled detection system deployed at Changi Airport to help keep our runways safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In the past, daily manual inspections were needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Now, staff can also rely on the round-the-clock automated scanning of foreign objects on our runways, which enable them to remove these objects quickly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling, Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Sharael Taha and Ms Mariam Jaafar asked how we are assisting our enterprises, especially our SMEs, to benefit from AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Derrick Goh and Mr Christopher de Souza sent the gist of their cuts to us separately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: They will be pleased to know that we are committed to accelerating AI adoption among SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are updating the Industry Digital Plans (IDPs) to include sector-specific AI tools and training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have done so for the retail, security, built environment, legal and tourism sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will update more IDPs this year, such as for the food services and hotel sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Of the approximately 300 pre-approved solutions supported by PSG, about 30% or a third of them are AI-enabled.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And last year, we launched the Gen AI Sandbox, allowing SMEs to experiment with 13 Gen AI solutions to improve their marketing and sales, and streamline customer engagement efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: One of the over 150 participants is AHA Inspiration, a health and wellness service platform provider.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: By integrating a Gen AI chatbot into its website and mobile application, AHA's employees can now handle customer inquiries almost twice as fast as before while providing more personalised customer service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: AHA Inspiration is just one of 120 SMEs that continued using the Gen AI solutions after the three-month Sandbox period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Our experience with the Sandbox reinforced the importance of providing opportunities for SMEs to discover the value of Gen AI through experimentation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Building on this success, IMDA launched Gen AI Sandbox 2.0 with 14 solutions in December last year to support a wider range of Gen AI solutions in areas, such as Generative Web Design, enabling SMEs to create websites using prompts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: SMEs can also try Gen AI tools for HR operations to create job descriptions and schedule interviews more efficiently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: If these Gen AI solutions prove useful, we intend to add them to the list of pre-approved solutions so that all SMEs can benefit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We also received feedback that it could be useful for the Sandbox to offer sector-specific solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: IMDA is happy to work with interested sector leads and industry associations on curating these solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Besides broad-based support for all SMEs, we are tapping on the capabilities of technology giants through the Gen AI x Digital Leaders (Gen AI x DL) programme to accelerate Gen AI adoption among the more digitally-mature enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These enterprises may require customised solutions that off-the-shelf products do not fully address.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To date, over 120 enterprises have used resources provided by tech giants and their partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: A quarter of them are working to build and deploy these solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Take, for example, iHub Solutions, a third-party logistics service provider. iHub's employees grappled with high volumes of ad hoc requests for reports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The time taken to manually create these reports hindered efficiency and reports were often error-prone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: During the programme, iHub leveraged the expertise of tech partners to develop a report generation tool using AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To seize opportunities to deploy Gen AI solutions at scale, IMDA will expand the Gen AI x DL partnerships to leverage tech partners' new development tools and pre-packaged software modules to deploy solutions for common use cases more quickly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is being piloted and we will share more details when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling also asked how the Government can encourage more enterprises to adopt Gen AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We recognise that enterprises face different challenges in doing so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For enterprises just starting to explore Gen AI, the Playbook illustrates the benefits of Gen AI through examples and offers resources on Gen AI solutions for specific needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For those deciding between buying off-the-shelf solutions and building proprietary ones, it provides an evaluation framework and information on associated risks to help them make informed choices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And for digitally-matured enterprises seeking more customised solutions, the Playbook provides insights on tech capabilities and partners needed to ensure successful implementation, alongside potential risks and governance considerations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Chairman, please allow me to speak in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: (In Mandarin):   With the Government's support and promotion, over 80% of SMEs are now successfully riding the digital wave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These businesses, spanning various sectors, have adopted at least one digital solution in their operations and achieved positive results.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Many businesses have also discovered that AI can help them reduce costs and enhance efficiency, thereby alleviating their cost pressures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To benefit more businesses, the Government will refresh the Industry Digital Plans for different sectors, providing more AI solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the same time, we will launch the new GenAI Playbook for Enterprises and Navigator, to recommend Generative AI tools and training suited to their needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Interested businesses can visit the CTO-as-a-Service platform for details.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The growing adoption of AI has significantly impacted our work and lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Local businesses and workers must keep pace to remain competitive and avoid falling behind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Therefore, I urge everyone to catch up and make full use of the Government's support and resources to level up digital capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Only then can we seize the opportunities brought forth by technological development and distinguish ourselves from the competition. : Chairman, as enterprises digitalise, they will be more exposed to cyber threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked how we are helping our enterprises stay safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: CSA's SG Cyber Safe programme provides differentiated support for enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As a baseline, CSA provides resources for various enterprise stakeholders, such as SME owners, employees and cybersecurity personnel.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Enterprises looking to implement cybersecurity measures can refer to the Cyber Essentials and Cyber Trust certification marks, which were developed as national cybersecurity standards in 2022.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To assist enterprises that need help with cybersecurity certification, CSA launched the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)-as-a-Service scheme in 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It onboards cybersecurity consultants to help enterprises develop cybersecurity health plans to implement the preventive measures in Cyber Essentials.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This has benefited over 270 enterprises and we will continue to do more to improve enterprise cyber hygiene standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We aligned SMEs Go Digital with the Cyber Essentials mark last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Under the pre-approved solutions, SMEs can now subscribe to an integrated package covering anti-malware, firewall and backup.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We also required pre-approved solutions under SMEs Go Digital to meet minimum data protection and security controls standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Going forward, CSA will expand Cyber Essentials and Cyber Trust in the first half of 2025 to cover the security of digital technologies, like cloud and AI, keeping them relevant for the evolving digital landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Besides uplifting standards, CSA will introduce a post-incident reporting and response function on CISO-as-a-Service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It is more important for enterprises to be resilient and recover from incidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Under this new function, enterprises can approach their CISO-as-a-Service consultants to help contain and recover from cybersecurity incidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Members can refer to the handout for a summary of our enterprise digitalisation and cybersecurity efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, many of us would find it hard to imagine our lives without the Internet or digital devices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In a survey conducted by MDDI in 2023, 80% of respondents agreed it was important for them to stay connected to the Internet.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There are healthy ways of using digital technologies to enhance our lives, just as there are unhealthy ways that open us up to risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: My speech will focus on MDDI's efforts to galvanise our community, to build a society where citizens enjoy access to digital services that are essential to daily living; proficiency in using digital technologies; and safe, healthy and positive digital experiences through a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singapore is a highly connected nation; 98% of our resident households are connected to the Internet.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: But we must pay attention to those who are at risk of being left out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Ms Hany Soh asked for an update on IMDA's schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond connectivity and devices, day-to-day digital services need to be user-friendly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For some Singaporeans, like seniors and persons with disabilities, navigating services which are not designed to meet their needs can be challenging.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A well-designed website or app can make a world of difference.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: That is why Singpass was enhanced in 2022 to support features, such as Dark Mode and Screen Reader, that enable those with visual impairments to navigate Singpass with greater ease.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Alex Yam asked about more efforts in this area.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Government takes inclusive design seriously and Government agencies are expected to be user-centric when designing their digital services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The updated DSS will better explain international standards, like the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), to agencies and provide recommendations on how to meet these standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In addition, there will be greater emphasis on user testing before launch for high-traffic Government websites to make sure they are user-friendly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have also rolled out tools that agencies can use to support inclusive design.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, GovTech developed the Oobee tool, previously known as Purple A11y, which uses a bot to help agencies test how easy their websites are to use and suggest improvements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: GovTech will continue to enhance tools to help agencies identify and resolve such issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These efforts provide agencies with stronger guidance and support to develop digital services that are easy for all to use, regardless of age or digital ability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: GovTech will provide dedicated support to agencies with high traffic digital services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: But the Government cannot drive this effort alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, Singaporeans use a variety of commercial digital services daily.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The private sector plays an important part in designing user-friendly digital services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We want to encourage and partner them in this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Oobee tool, which I mentioned earlier, is open-sourced and freely available for private sector companies to use.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We encourage more to make use of this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Last year, GovTech held the inaugural Co-Creation Lab, which brought together representatives from Government agencies, private sector companies as well as community users.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We were heartened to see so many partners step forward to understand the challenges that seniors and persons with disabilities face when using digital services, such as making e-payments, using ride-hailing apps and making healthcare appointments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These conversations helped service providers identify improvements to their services to make them user-friendly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Co-Creation Lab demonstrated the need to strengthen partnerships across the public, private and people sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Details on this workgroup will be announced later.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Even as we enhance the user-friendliness of digital services, we acknowledge that some Singaporeans will need physical support to access Government services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng and Ms Denise Phua highlighted this in the Budget debate and Mr Gerald Giam raised this in his cut.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Residents who need assistance with Government digital transactions can continue to get in-person assistance at Government agencies' physical service touchpoints.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Trained service ambassadors will assist less digitally confident individuals with their transactions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Residents can also visit ServiceSG centres for assistance with 600 frequently used Government services and schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Government will continue to be citizen-centric in our approach and make non-digital options available so that no one is left out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To set ourselves up well for the digital future, Singaporeans also have to learn new technologies, such as Gen AI, which can help us with daily tasks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This upskilling is critical, as Ms Denise Phua emphasised in the Budget debate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Without this, the increasing use of Gen AI around us, like how many businesses now use chatbots to deliver customer services, can feel alien and scary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To demystify Gen AI, we must understand its risks and limitations and learn how to use it responsibly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Government will continue to support less digitally-savvy citizens.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Gerald Giam and Ms Hany Soh asked about Seniors Go Digital.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The SG Digital Office (SDO) will continue to help citizens acquire the digital skills needed for day-to-day living based on the Digital Skills for Life (DSL) framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This prevents digital isolation, as Miss Rachel Ong raised in the Budget debate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Interested learners can register for SDO workshops or learn at their own pace through resources on the Digital for Life Portal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There are also many Singaporeans who are keen to embrace new technologies like AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Alex Yam asked about new library initiatives to encourage tech adoption.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Over the next few years, our public libraries will be rolling out showcases that allow the public to experience uses of Gen AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We hope that these showcases will demonstrate the practical value of AI in daily life, excite citizens about these possibilities and at the same time, help them understand the limitations and learn how to use AI responsibly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Gen AI is a useful tool, but it cannot replace learning or original thought.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These are just some of the activities that citizens can enjoy at our public libraries as National Library Board (NLB) celebrates its 30th anniversary in 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: NLB will host a series of "NLB30" events to mark 30 years and beyond of empowering Singaporeans to read, learn and discover together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: More details will be announced later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: (In Malay):   One of the best ways for us to learn to use cutting-edge technology is to do it together with like-minded individuals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A pioneering initiative that creates opportunities for communities to gather and learn together is Lorong AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is a community hub that provides space for those who share similarities, interests and skills in AI to explore how they can drive AI development together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through this platform, they exchange ideas and discuss the latest discoveries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They also create prototypes and explore the use of AI in our daily lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Muhammad Zahari bin Abu Talib plays a crucial role in Lorong AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As Community Lead, he helps connect individuals, initiates discussions and links various groups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I personally felt their enthusiasm for learning, sharing and collaborating when I attended one of the AI Wednesdays sharing sessions organised by Lorong AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Within our Malay/Muslim community, many have already begun exploring AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A group called PEREKA, comprising Malay/Muslim designers from various fields, shared how they use AI to improve their work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I had the opportunity to meet them recently, and was very excited to hear how they leverage AI to enhance their work processes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The aim is not to replace human creativity, but to facilitate the ideation process and gather information.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: All this is to produce design features that align with our cultural values and identity and at the same time, ensuring that the human touch remains at the core throughout the design process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I really hope that more dynamic local groups like these will emerge so that they can learn together and spark interesting ideas to harness technology for the well-being of Singaporeans. : Mr Chairman, let me now turn to how we are equipping the future generation to benefit from Gen AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have an existing Code for Fun programme offered to all primary and secondary schools, which exposes students to computational thinking through coding as well as inventive thinking through digital making.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: From this year onwards, the Code for Fun programme will incorporate new AI for Fun modules, which provide students with hands-on opportunities to tinker with AI technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For instance, primary school students will be taught how to use an appropriate Gen AI platform to generate stories and images to create a digital storyboard.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Students will be taught the risks of Gen AI, such as biases and hallucinations, and the need to check AI-generated content against other sources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is our endeavour to ensure that every Singaporean, regardless of age, is encouraged to learn, use and have fun with new technologies in an informed and responsible way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This brings me to the topic of online safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Incidents that take place online, like the generation and dissemination of deepfake nude photos, cause real-life damage and are unacceptable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This has led some people to be fearful of the Internet and how it appears to be changing the fabric of our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: But it is important to recognise that these harms are not caused by technology in itself, but by bad actors and bad behaviour.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Government will do our part to reduce online risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Minister Josephine Teo earlier spoke about our regulations to make designated social media services and app distribution services responsible for putting in place safety measures to protect their users from harmful content.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Citizens must also take steps to protect themselves and their loved ones online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Parents play a critical role in guiding their child's digital journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Government shares parents' concerns over excessive screen use and exposure to online risks amongst children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Parents can also find bite-sized resources on IMDA's Digital for Life portal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Members may refer to the handout for a list of these resources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A Positive Use Guide on Technology and Social Media will also be available later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Youths are a key group of citizens who shape online behaviour and culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Youths should be encouraged to use their influence to foster a positive online environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I was encouraged to see students championing a kinder Internet at a recent digital well-being roadshow at the Singapore Management University.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One booth featured an interactive game that showed participants how to navigate online conversations and respond to their friends with care and kindness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Toxic online discourse is worrying because it undermines our ability to understand one another and disrupts our social cohesion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As Mr Alex Yam mentioned, we must be civic-minded in the online space, just as how we conduct ourselves in our shared physical spaces like our neighbourhoods, parks and schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In the work that the Government does, it is always important to check in on the sentiments of the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This allows us to accurately identify Singaporeans' concerns and align with the expectation for a responsive Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Gerald Giam shared his experience with surveys and asked if they were commissioned by the Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is unfortunate that the poster did not disclose to Mr Giam the identity of the commissioning party for the survey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Without the benefit of seeing the actual questionnaire, it is difficult to say for sure that the surveys were conducted by the Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: When asked by respondents, our representatives would identify MDDI as the commissioning agency for the surveys.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We conduct the media polls to help Government agencies adjust their public communication efforts to better reach target segments on key national policies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They also help shape our public broadcast funding.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The poll findings on scams help MDDI to shape our policies to tackle online harm.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister of State Rahayu, you might want to round up.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The findings from the Government-commissioned surveys are shared publicly when it is useful to do so.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: However, as the surveys are commissioned primarily to shape public policy, not all findings are suitable for public release.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As to Mr Giam's concern that Government-commissioned surveys could be used for non-public policy purposes, funding for such surveys is subject to the same governance requirements as other forms of public expenditure undertaken by Government agencies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To conclude, Mr Chairman, we invite everyone – individuals, companies and community organisations – to become a partner of the Digital for Life movement and join us in our efforts to help Singapore build an inclusive and cohesive digital society.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: All of us have a part to play in making our online space a safe, healthy and positive one.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: First of all, it is heartening to hear of the many measures put in place to protect Singaporeans better from online harms.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I would also like to find out what more will be done or has been done so far to protect citizens from scams so that they will feel safe, competent and more confident to interact and transact online, which is also part of the trust that we talked about.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Lastly, picking up on the point on funding vernacular media, I think vernacular media has a strategic part to play, especially in projecting Singapore's voice and opinion on key issues internationally.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Zaobao, for example, has a very strong presence and network in certain areas or regions.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: It has been very useful in asserting our point of view.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: So, I would like to ask whether the funding support in this area will be continued or strengthened and what else might we be doing to boost this so that we can strengthen Singapore's position on the world stage.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, I would, first, like to thank Ms Tin for her acknowledgement of our efforts and in particular, her recognition of the importance of preserving our vernacular media.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If we think about the need to continue projecting Singapore's voice on the international stage, in fact, the role of the vernacular media becomes even more prominent.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I wish to recognise her acknowledgement and affirm it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The big chunk of the Public Service Media funding support is directed towards helping our Public Service Media entities become more relevant in the digital era, so the technology upgrades are essential to this.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But we have always maintained that at the same time we want to support quality journalism and that cuts across all language medium.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And in particular, recognising that the domestic market for our vernacular media is actually very small, they need extra support.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the understanding with the public service media entities is that they must set aside adequate resources, and the KPIs do track the performance of the vernacular media.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think that how they do on the KPIs is not just a matter of looking at their performance, but it is also a matter of helping us understand how the landscape is changing and what more is required to support the continued viability of vernacular media.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do so broadly in two ways, first by disrupting and making it harder for scammers to reach Singaporeans, whether by calls, SMSes, or apps infected with malware, because that is really how the victims fall.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is what we, within the working group, call the "attack factor".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Second, by developing technology to support MHA's detection and disruption of scam activities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, those are the two main areas of support.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I am sure we have all gotten them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: IMDA also partnered with telcos to strengthen in network detection and blocking of scam calls and SMSes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They were about 25% of all international calls.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: IMDA also worked with telcos to offer new features to block all incoming international calls and SMSes, meaning that from the subscriber standpoint, I do not want to be at risk at all, I do not want to just depend on your auto blocking, I do not wish to get any of these calls.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And to date, more than 280,000 subscribers have activated the feature to block overseas calls and close to 220,000 subscribers have activated the feature to block overseas SMSes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If I add GovTech's working with the Singapore Police Force (SPF) to disrupt 45,000 scam related websites and also IMDA working with SPF to disrupt more than 57,000 mobile lines assessed to be likely used for scams, these are very considerable efforts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But we are not stopping at the above measures.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are working with telcos and online platforms to address criminal misuse of their services.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I hope replies will also be short because I can see quite a few hands.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I really want everyone to keep your replies and responses short.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: According to DeepSeek, there are hardware and software optimisations that have brought down the training and inference costs, and then by extension, this makes the compute greener because less energy is needed, a fraction of the compute.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If it is true, and seeing as the company has made their model open source, there is indeed a possible positive development for advancing the efforts around resource efficient AI.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: However, there are counter claims that the actual compute cluster may have been much larger than reported and there may have been distillation of closed models.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the facts around the matter are unclear, and we are still studying the matter to learn how best we can deploy compute power here in Singapore to advance our ambitions.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank Minister Teo and the team for answering the cuts.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: The annex distributed mentions the recommendation to purchase IoT devices with the CSA cybersecurity labelling scheme.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: And given that added compliance cost and the upcoming carbon tax, could this drive companies to set up data centres elsewhere, making the timeline for studying alternative energy sources even more urgent for us?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: And lastly, my last question was something that was not answered in the response.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: For Senior Minister of State Tan, in Budget 2024, it was announced that there would be collaborations with industry to drive AI adoption and innovation.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Can the Ministry provide an update on these collaborations with the industry, please?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Yes, there is one for Senior Minister of State Janil and one for Senior Minister of State Tan.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Essentially, whether or not the push for green data centres will affect our global competitiveness and drive up costs, indeed, we have to balance the compliance costs with the requirements.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But there is plenty of interest in the market and if we can get this right, then this is a value-add and a potential source of competitiveness that we can be a place where the technology providers, the cloud service providers can set up greener facilities, and their customers are looking for this type of solutions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, while we do have to make sure that we get the balance correct between the costs of compliance and the push for greening, it is something that we have to do because of our larger issues around our carbon envelope.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But if we can do it right, it becomes a source of competitiveness for us.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The partners include, for example, the Singapore Business Federation, Microsoft, Salesforce, Amazon Web Services, DBS Bank, as well as the Singapore Computer Society and SG Tech.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: They also delivered AI and data analytics workshops for nearly 1,000 SMEs, helping them thrive in today's technology driven business environment.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And we will continue expanding our network of partnership.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, Mr Sharael Taha will be pleased to know that we will be sharing upcoming collaborations with new partners, for example, with Alibaba Cloud to raise capabilities of solution providers in AI and cloud technologies, and another one with ST Engineering to improve cyber resilience amongst SMEs.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, we welcome more partners to join us to create a robust ecosystem where enterprises and workers can thrive.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Sorry, Minister Teo, you want to jump in now?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, in the nature of such botnet disruption operations, speed is of the essence and you want to be as comprehensive as possible.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, with those important considerations in mind, it is not possible to attempt even to inform all of the owners of the devices.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Instead, what we regularly advise people to do is that as long as you have a device that is connected to the Internet, there are some hygiene practices that should be practised: changing the default password, restarting or rebooting regularly and enabling automatic firmware updates.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These are the general guidance that apply to everyone.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And in cybersecurity there is also another term that we say and that is "assume breach".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is something that you just have to keep in mind.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: You have to be vigilant and assume that the device may well have been compromised, and you need to do something to clean it up regularly.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I do not think there is anything untoward about that.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The question that was the nub of the issue I was seeking to raise was on KPIs, which is the title of the cut.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: If I heard the Minister correctly, Minister said that reach is an important KPI, but not the only KPI.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And I stand corrected if I am wrong, Minister then said that trust and satisfaction levels are KPIs that the Ministry was looking to introduce.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, can I confirm that those KPIs actually are not KPIs that are considered currently?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, when we set out to provide funding to any useful activity, we have to consider in that moment what are useful and effective ways to track performance and we do so very diligently.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To the Member's question that he posed in his cut earlier, I should address it briefly too.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He had asked about what goes into the Budget book.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And I acknowledge his suggestions, which we will consider for the future, but just to say that, like all Ministries, it is not possible to list all of the KPIs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The important thing is that where SMT is concerned, they know very well that the KPIs are a very central feature of the conversations that we have, and they can feel it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, that is something I want to say.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The comparison between ST and CNA, well, the fact of the matter is that opinions will differ.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you ask 10 people their views, probably you will get 15 at least.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I think we take that as a given.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We track how the public views the trustworthiness of these titles and we will continue to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And as I shared in my speech, as well as on other occasions, they compare very favourably.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: She spoke at length earlier about the NLB as well as adoption of AI.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: As we know, AI is quite ubiquitous today, so how will NLB ensure that the adoption of AI remains respectful towards authors and content creators, and of course not diminish the value of creativity and hard work in coming out with content?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Indeed, NLB sees Gen AI as a useful tool and seeks to provide the platforms and opportunities for both to be edified about it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But we are also respectful of the different interests.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We do see strong public interest in the different AI prototypes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This ensures that AI is used ethically and responsibly to complement, not replace, the efforts of authors and creators.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Through such prototypes, NLB also hopes to help visitors discover writers, stories and content and experience them in different ways.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Can I confirm that all Government agencies are expected to provide in-person assistance for their e-services?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Second, can the Minister of State also confirm that all pollsters engaged by the Government are expected to disclose that they were commissioned by the Government and name the agency without being requested by the respondent?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Lastly, can the Ministry also look into publishing at least summaries of these public opinion surveys?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Chairman, let me take the second and third questions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: They will have different needs and may address different issues.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It may be that, for some surveys, there may be a preference to have it as anonymised in that sense because the response, if you are told that it is something that is asked by the Government, may then not be accurate and may be skewed because if you are asked, say, for benefits, whether they should be improved or increased, without assessing the situation, the person might just respond because it is the Government, expecting that it should be changed, to just ask for more.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, I think there are certain considerations which I would not want to assume, because different agencies may do it differently.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On the Member's third question, all surveys are done in the interest of the public.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is really, where possible, if the information that is garnered from those surveys is useful, we would want to put it up.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We want to be as rich as possible so as to encourage public discussion.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But there are certain matters that may not be as suitable.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There may be certain sensitivities in issues of, say, racial and religious issues, if we have done surveys on that and certain matters come up.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And there may be certain understanding or contracts that we may have with certain agencies that we partner in doing some of those surveys.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, there are different considerations for different surveys and, therefore, there is a different approach.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I think we endeavour as much as possible to make sure that there are alternatives and support.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Like I said, we set up the ServiceSG centres for the purposes of that.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As much as possible, we will endeavour to make sure that those who are in need, who are unable to access it, will be able to get the help they need.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And I think that can be done in many different forms.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, if there are concerns highlighted to us, we will see how we can close those gaps.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I am sorry, we have run out of time, Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Ong Hua Han.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have sat in here for almost five hours.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 2.51 pm until 3.10 pm.
